proof.text:
Suppose $S_r(M)=\tau_r(M)$. The inverse identities for $d_{r,M}$ and functoriality of $H$ give $H(d_{r,M})\circ S_r(M)=E_r(M)$. Naturality of $\eta$, applied to the morphism $d_{r,M}:P_rM\to T^rM$, says
$$\eta_{T^rM}\circ H(d_{r,M})=H(T(d_{r,M}))\circ\eta_{P_rM}.$$
Substitute this into the definition of $S_{r+1}$, use the assumed coherence $d_{r+1,M}^{-1}\circ T(d_{r,M})=b_{r,M}$, and use preservation of composition by $H$. With composition reassociated by [def-nagata-category], this gives
$$\begin{aligned}
S_{r+1}(M)&=H(d_{r+1,M}^{-1})\circ\eta_{T^rM}\circ E_r(M)\\
&=H(d_{r+1,M}^{-1})\circ H(T(d_{r,M}))\circ\eta_{P_rM}\circ S_r(M)\\
&=H(b_{r,M})\circ\eta_{P_rM}\circ\tau_r(M)=\tau_{r+1}(M).
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate substitution uses the induction hypothesis; the last equality is the given recurrence. In particular, no naturality of the maps $\tau_r$ is required.

title: Formal induction for repeated natural transport
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], let $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be functors, and let $P_r:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be functors for $r\geq1$, with $P_1=T$. Put $T^0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, $T^1=T$ and $T^{r+1}=T\circ T^r$, using canonical functor associators. Suppose there are natural isomorphisms $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ and $b_r:T\circ P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{r+1}$ with $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $d_{r+1}^{-1}\circ T(d_r)=b_r$, and a natural transformation $\eta:H\Rightarrow H\circ T$. For maps $\tau_r(M):H(M)\to H(P_rM)$ assume $\tau_1(M)=\eta_M$ and
$$\tau_{r+1}(M)=H(b_{r,M})\circ\eta_{P_rM}\circ\tau_r(M).$$
Define
$$S_r(M)=H(d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\eta_{T^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\eta_M.$$
Then $S_r(M)=\tau_r(M)$ for every $r\geq1$ and $M$.
Here a functor assigns objects and morphisms and preserves identities and composition. A natural transformation $\alpha:F\Rightarrow G$ is a family $\alpha_M:F(M)\to G(M)$ satisfying $G(u)\circ\alpha_M=\alpha_N\circ F(u)$ for each $u:M\to N$; it is a natural isomorphism when every component is invertible.
